name: Onesiphorus
title: The Faithful Friend from Ephesus
summary: Onesiphorus was a faithful Christian from Ephesus known for his devotion to the apostle Paul. He sought out Paul while he was imprisoned in Rome and was not ashamed of the apostle's chains. Paul mentions him with deep gratitude and prays that the Lord may show mercy to his household.

keyEvents.title: Service in Ephesus
keyEvents.description: Onesiphorus served Paul and the church in many ways while he was in Ephesus, something Timothy knew well.

keyEvents.title: Sought Out Paul in Rome
keyEvents.description: When Onesiphorus arrived in Rome, he diligently searched for Paul and found him, even though the apostle was in captivity.

keyEvents.title: Not Ashamed of Paul's Chains
keyEvents.description: Unlike others who abandoned Paul, Onesiphorus was not ashamed of the apostle's imprisonment but showed him faithful care.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Prayer for Mercy on His Household
keyEvents.description: Paul prayed that the Lord would show mercy to Onesiphorus' household as a reward for his faithful service.

keyEvents.title: Greeting to the Household of Onesiphorus
keyEvents.description: In the conclusion of his second letter to Timothy, Paul sends greetings to the household of Onesiphorus, which testifies to the close bond between them.

keyEvents.title: Contrast with Those Who Deserted Paul
keyEvents.description: Onesiphorus is mentioned in contrast to Phygelus and Hermogenes and others in Asia who turned away from Paul, thus appearing as a model of faithful friendship.
